business.title: Molecular locking of lithium ions for improved efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells
business.desc: The hole-transport material 2,2′,7,7′-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenyl-amine)-9,9′-spirobifluorene (Spiro-OMeTAD) is commonly used in perovskite solar cells but suffers from instabilities due to the hygroscopicity and lithium ion migration induced by additives, such as lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and 4-tert-butylpyridine (tBP), in its formulation. Here we show a molecular locking strategy by designing phosphonate-based molecules with extended cyano chains, enabling dual-site coordination with lithium ions to regulate ion mobility and stabilize the lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide/tBP dopant environment. Meanwhile, the phosphonate-based molecule reduces tBP loss, enhances the thermomechanical robustness of the Spiro-OMeTAD matrix, mitigates dopant redistribution and stabilizes the interface. These coupled effects collectively improve device stability under illumination, thermal and electrical stresses. The optimized n–i–p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion efficiency of 26.73% and retain 95% of the initial efficiency after 1,000 h under maximum power point tracking (International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS)-L-1), 95% after 1,000 h at 85 °C (ISOS-L-2) and 91% after 1,600 h under 1.5 V bias (ISOS-V-1). Spiro-OMeTAD is a common hole-transporting material in n–i–p perovskite solar cells but suffers from instabilities caused by mobile lithium dopant ions. Pan et al. incorporate a molecular locking additive in Spiro-OMeTAD, enhancing both the efficiency and stability of devices.

business.title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air
business.desc: Direct air capture combined with electrosynthesis could turn atmospheric CO2 into fuels, but releasing tightly bound CO2 from capture liquids demands intense heat, and the resulting end-to-end energy burden exceeds 35 GJ per tonne of CO. Electrified reactive capture avoids thermal regeneration by feeding capture liquid directly into an electrolyser, yet reported systems remain energy-intensive and typically fail within 100 h. Here we show that these failures trace to proton management: too large a flux of protons crossing the membrane acidifies the cathode and degrades the catalyst, while too small a flux starves proton-driven in situ CO2 release, both favouring hydrogen evolution. We define the proton transference number ( $${{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}$$ ), the fraction of ionic current carried by protons, as a quantitative descriptor linking ion transport to CO selectivity, carbon utilization and durability. Replacing oxygen evolution with gas-fed hydrogen oxidation at the anode maintains $${{{t}}}_{{{\rm{H}}}^{+}}\approx 1$$ , enabling 1,000 h of stable operation at ~1 V and 100 mA cm−2, and CO production from air at 22 GJ t−1 with >90% carbon utilization. Direct air capture integrated with electrosynthesis to produce fuels and chemicals is hindered by high energy consumption and limited operational lifetimes. Here the authors identify proton management as crucial for stability and achieve 1,000 h of stable operation by using gas-fed hydrogen oxidation at the anode, which maintains ideal ion transport and enhances CO production.

business.title: Vibration characteristics of a tracked combine harvester chassis frame during progressive component engagement and field operation
business.desc: The chassis frame of a tracked combine harvester is subjected to periodic excitation from the engine and working components together with random excitation from the crawler–ground interaction. This study combined a stationary progressive-superposition test with a supplementary field-operational test to compare changes associated with component engagement and describe vibration during field operation. In the stationary test, triaxial accelerations were measured at four excitation-source supports and four chassis-frame locations under six working conditions. Root mean square (RMS), fast Fourier transform (FFT), and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) analyses identified vibration intensity, dominant frequencies, and energy evolution. Engagement of the threshing and cleaning system increased the three-axis averaged RMS acceleration at monitoring point 6 from 4.02 to 15.21 m/s2 and increased the amplitudes of components near 157–158 Hz at several monitoring points. In the field test, all working components and the traveling system operated simultaneously, with a triaxial accelerometer mounted on the outer face of the crawler beam at monitoring point 6. After conversion to the machine coordinate system, the longitudinal, lateral, and vertical RMS accelerations were 2.44, 3.92, and 6.37 m/s2, respectively. The vertical direction was dominant, with major power spectral density peaks at 15.63 and 31.25 Hz. The stationary tests show how vibration changed as components were engaged. The single field measurement characterizes the combined response at the crawler beam during harvesting.

technology.title: MRI assessment of masseter muscle volume in temporomandibular joint anterior disc displacement
technology.desc: This study aimed to evaluate volumetric differences in the masseter muscle in individuals with anterior disc displacement of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), with and without reduction, using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This retrospective cross-sectional study included MRI records of 279 individuals aged 18–69 years (median age: 24 years; Q1–Q3: 19–40 years). Participants were classified into three disc-status categories: normal disc position, anterior disc displacement with reduction (DDwR), and anterior disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). Bilateral TMJs and their corresponding masseter muscles were evaluated, yielding 558 side-specific TMJ–masseter observations. Masseter muscle volumes were measured on coronal T2-weighted MRI images in the closed-mouth position using semi-automated segmentation with ITK-SNAP software by a blinded observer. Intraobserver and interobserver reliability were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Statistical analyses included the Shapiro–Wilk and Kruskal–Wallis tests, Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction, and a linear mixed-effects model accounting for within-patient correlation between bilateral measurements. TMJ disc status was significantly associated with ipsilateral masseter muscle volume in the linear mixed-effects model after adjustment for age, sex, side, and within-patient correlation (F(2, 292.244) = 52.818, p < 0.001). Compared with TMJs showing disc displacement without reduction, masseter muscle volume was higher in TMJs with normal disc position (β = 2.018 cm3, 95% CI 1.628–2.409) and with disc displacement with reduction (β = 0.696 cm3, 95% CI 0.310–1.081). Exploratory sex-stratified analyses suggested differences in the patterns of association, while strong positive correlations between right and left masseter muscle volumes were observed across the examined subgroups. MRI-defined anterior disc displacement of the TMJ, particularly without reduction, was associated with lower masseter muscle volume. These findings demonstrate an association rather than a causal relationship and should be interpreted considering the retrospective design and unavailable functional or parafunctional clinical information.

technology.title: Exploring nonlinear body oscillations for natural quadruped gaits
technology.desc: Animals’ body morphology shapes the gait patterns they can perform, where mechanical resonance reduces the need for active control. By tuning posture and muscle stiffness, they leverage their embodied intelligence to achieve effective gaits for different speeds. By contrast, most quadruped robots are not specifically designed to exploit mechanical resonance owing to the complexity of nonlinear dynamics and require dedicated locomotion controllers. To provide an alternative, we present a proof-of-concept framework making the nonlinear dynamics of a robot predictable in the design process and show how this knowledge can be leveraged such that multi-gait locomotion can emerge from nonlinear resonances—shaped by gravity, inertia and elasticity. Here we present the highly compliant quadruped robot eBert, on which we identify six nonlinear normal modes using our new theoretical tools and validate their existence in simulation and hardware. With black-box optimization to determine step length, simulations show how each nonlinear normal mode naturally develops into a distinct gait, manifesting different speeds, which also largely transfers to the robotic hardware. Our experiments show that eBert can exploit its mechanics to generate task-specific movements, which may serve as foundation for designing a new generation of agile and efficient robots leveraging embodied intelligence. Schmidt et al. demonstrate that nonlinear normal modes can be used to develop natural, multi-gait locomotion in a compliant quadruped robot, leveraging its inherent mechanics. The approach offers a design tool to shape embodied intelligence in robotics.

technology.title: Estimation of renewable energy consumption and its determinants for OECD countries using biased estimators
technology.desc: Renewable energy consumption is influenced by factors, including trade dynamics, foreign direct investment, labor market conditions, industrial development, fossil fuel dependence, and population structure. Therefore, this study is modeled by a linear regression model for renewable energy consumption in OECD countries. The model utilizes several determinants of renewable energy consumption, including exports, foreign direct investment, labor force, industrialization, fossil fuel energy consumption, life expectancy, carbon dioxide emissions, imports, gross domestic product per capita and urban population. Data from 2021 regarding these variables are analyzed for 38 OECD countries. However, the model established for OECD countries has a multicollinearity problem, making it unstable with classical estimators. Biased estimators must be used for model estimation. Accordingly, Ordinary Least Square (OLS), Ridge and Generalized Maximum Entropy (GME) estimators are used, and the estimators are compared according to the Mean Squared Error criterion. In this study, we obtained that increases in exports, industrialization, fossil fuel energy consumption, and urban population lead to an increase in renewable energy consumption, whereas increases in carbon dioxide emissions, imports, and life expectancy at birth lead to a decrease in renewable energy consumption. Although some of the results may initially appear surprising, they stem from the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic (e.g., exports, urban population, carbon dioxide emissions, life expectancy at birth, etc.). Furthermore, findings for study show that the superiority of using the GME as a biased estimator in the presence of a multicollinearity problem. Therefore, for future research, the use of biased estimators—and the GME in particular—is recommended in situations where model assumptions are not met.
